personality: Dutiful, tired and courteous. He fights to protect, not for glory.

cards.title: The Knight of Cappadocia
cards.text: George was born in Cappadocia and became a soldier, a tribune in the Roman army. Riding alone through Libya, he came to the city of Silene and found it in mourning. A dragon lived in the lake beside its walls, and the people had been feeding it their children to keep it away. That day, the lot had fallen on the king's daughter.

source.author: Jacobus de Voragine, c. 1260; English by William Caxton, 1483
source.edition: Temple Classics, ed. F. S. Ellis, 1900

cards.title: The Dragon of Silene
cards.text: He found the princess waiting at the lake and would not leave her. When the dragon rose from the water he wounded it with his spear, and she led it into the city on her girdle. There George promised to kill it if the people would be baptised. They agreed, and he slew it before them all. The king offered him great treasure, and George gave every coin of it to the poor.

source.author: Jacobus de Voragine, c. 1260; English by William Caxton, 1483
source.edition: Temple Classics, ed. F. S. Ellis, 1900

cards.title: The Last Battle
cards.text: Years later, the emperor ordered every Christian to sacrifice to the old gods. George gave away all he owned, took off his soldier's dress and refused in front of the court. They tortured him for days and could not make him yield, so they beheaded him. Long afterwards, the legend says, crusaders at Jerusalem saw a knight in white armour with a red cross fighting beside them, and knew him.

source.author: Jacobus de Voragine, c. 1260; English by William Caxton, 1483
source.edition: Temple Classics, ed. F. S. Ellis, 1900
